title: Integrated Finance Playbook: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference’s standard operating procedures for annual budgeting and rolling forecasts, procurement and vendor contracting, purchase order (PO) controls, and revenue recognition / billing practices. It is intended for Finance, Legal, Procurement, and business owners who request spend, execute customer or vendor contracts, or own product pricing.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood entities and subsidiaries unless a customer-specific NDA or legal carve-out states otherwise. Exceptions require approval from Director of Finance and General Counsel.

Owner and escalation

- Primary owner: Finance (Director of Finance, Leah Morris)
- Legal owner: Legal Counsel (Carlos Vega)
- Procurement coordinator: Procurement Manager (Maya Singh)
- Escalation: Finance leadership -> General Counsel -> CFO for material exceptions (> $250,000)

1) Annual budgeting and rolling forecasting

Summary: Redwood uses a top-down annual operating plan (AOP) with quarterly reforecasts and a 12-month rolling forecast updated monthly. The budgeting process balances headcount, cloud and GPU capacity commitments, sales quotas, and GTM investments.

Key timelines and deliverables:
- Budget kickoff: September 15 (planning deck and headcount assumptions)
- Draft budgets due: October 31 (departmental P&Ls submitted in template)
- Finance consolidation and review: Nov 1-15
- Executive review and approval: Nov 20-30
- Board review: December board packet
- Rolling forecast cadence: monthly updates submitted by the 5th business day of each month

Inputs and assumptions:
- Headcount model (FTEs, hiring lags, salary bands)
- Cloud/GPU capacity commitments and committed spend for Dedicated contracts
- Sales pipeline and bookings conversion rates (sales qualifies forecast vs. closed won)
- Historical burn and cost per token estimates for hosted API usage
- FX and cross-border tax assumptions for regional expansions

Templates and controls:
- Use the Finance departmental P&L template (Drive link in related pages).
- All material changes (>10% variance vs. prior approved budget line or >$100k) require a written variance explanation and approval from Finance Director.

2) Procurement and vendor onboarding

Purpose: Standardize vendor selection, PO issuance, approvals, and vendor risk assessment.

Approval thresholds:
- < $5,000: Team lead approval (email ok)
- $5,000- $25,000: Department head approval + Procurement notification
- $25,000- $250,000: Procurement Manager + Finance Controller signoff; obtain at least 3 competitive quotes where practicable
- > $250,000: Procurement Manager + Director of Finance + General Counsel review and CFO approval

Vendor selection and risk assessment:
- All vendors must complete a Vendor Risk Assessment (VRA) for security, data residency, and business continuity. Procurement coordinates VRA with Security team for vendors accessing customer data or Redwood systems.
- For SaaS vendors with access to PII/customer data, require SOC2 Type II report and data processing addendum (DPA).

PO and invoice workflow:
- Requestors should submit a Procurement Request Form (PRF) with scope, budget code, and preferred vendor.
- Procurement issues PO via ERP system once approvals are in place. No work should start without an approved PO unless pre-authorized in writing by the Procurement Manager.
- Invoices must reference the PO and be routed to accounts-payable@redwood-inference.com for processing. Standard terms are Net 30 unless a different term is approved by Finance.

Payment terms and discounts:
- Standard vendor payment term: Net 30 from invoice receipt.
- Early payment discount: Accepted if positive NPV and approved by Finance Controller.
- For vendor prepayments or retention arrangements (> $100,000), obtain Treasurer sign-off and confirm reversal/escrow controls.

3) Contracts and legal process

Contract intake and routing:
- All vendor and customer contracts must be routed through the Contract Management System (CMS) and assigned to Legal using the Contract Intake Form.
- Non-standard terms (e.g., indemnity, data residency, IP assignments) must be flagged at intake and reviewed by Legal.

Contract signatory limits:
- Individual contributors: no signatory authority
- Directors: sign up to $50,000 for vendor contracts with pre-approved templates
- VP level: sign up to $250,000 with Legal review
- CFO/CEO: signatory for amounts above $250,000 or strategic agreements (equity, JV, MSA)

Standard contract playbook and redlines:
- Use the approved template library in CMS. Legal maintains the single source of truth for standard vendor and customer Master Service Agreements (MSAs), SOW templates, DPAs, and reseller agreements.
- Typical customer MSA negotiation priorities:
  1. Limitations of liability (cap equal to total fees paid over 12 months)
  2. Service-level availability and remedies (credits vs. termination)
  3. Data security, breach notification timelines (48 hours for serious incidents), and data residency clauses
  4. IP ownership and license scope (customer data vs. model outputs)

Contract lifecycle management:
- Legal tags each executed contract with owner, renewal date, auto-renew terms, and termination windows in the CMS. Procurement monitors vendor contract expirations and negotiates renewals 90 days prior to expiry.

4) Revenue recognition and billing policy (high level)

Principles: Redwood recognizes revenue in accordance with ASC 606 (or applicable local equivalent). Revenue is recognized when (1) a contract with a customer exists, (2) performance obligations are identified, (3) the transaction price is determined, (4) the transaction price is allocated to performance obligations, and (5) revenue is recognized when obligations are satisfied.

Common product scenarios and treatment:
- Hosted API usage (metered tokens): Recognize revenue as usage occurs (over time) based on metered consumption. Invoices are issued monthly in arrears unless otherwise agreed.
- Dedicated capacity (committed reserved capacity): For non-cancellable, prepaid capacity, recognize revenue ratably over the committed term (deferred revenue on receipt). For committed usage with variable consumption, split fixed and variable consideration and recognize accordingly.
- Private deployments / on-prem: Recognize license fees based on contract terms; maintenance and support recognized ratably over the support period.
- Prepaid credits and prepayments: Record as deferred revenue on receipt and recognize as consumed or on a straight-line basis if consumption pattern is unknown but expected to be recognized within 12 months.

Billing cadence and invoicing standards:
- Standard billing: Monthly invoicing in arrears for metered services; annual invoices for committed capacity if customer elects annual billing.
- Invoice contents must include: customer name, contract/PO reference, period covered, usage detail (tokens/embedding units), unit price, discounts or credits, tax details, and payment instructions.
- Dispute handling: Customer disputes must be logged in the billing ticketing queue and responded to within 5 business days. Material disputes (> $25,000) escalate to Finance Director and Customer Success.

Deferred revenue management and cutoffs:
- Finance runs monthly cutoffs on the last business day of the month. Deferred revenue schedules are reconciled to the general ledger monthly and reviewed by the Controller.
- Material adjustments (> $50,000) to deferred revenue need a variance memo and Controller sign-off.

5) Controls, reporting, and KPIs

Controls:
- Segregation of duties: Requestor, approver, and Accounts Payable payment approver should be distinct individuals.
- Dual control for wire transfers above $100,000 (Treasurer + Finance Director).
- Contract redlines and non-standard concessions must be logged and reviewed quarterly by Legal and Finance.

KPIs and reporting:
- Monthly: Actual vs. budget (P&L), cash runway, deferred revenue schedule, days sales outstanding (DSO), PO cycle time, vendor spend by category
- Quarterly: Revenue growth, gross margin, ARR / bookings reconciliation, retention metrics tied to revenue classes

6) Templates, checklists, and quick reference

Included templates (links in CMS / Drive):
- Procurement Request Form (PRF) template
- Vendor Risk Assessment (VRA) checklist
- Standard MSA and SOW templates
- Finance departmental P&L template and rolling forecast workbook
- Contract Intake Form

Quick checklist for requestors:
1. Confirm budget code and available budget with Finance.
2. Complete PRF and attach 2-3 vendor quotes if > $25k.
3. Submit Contract Intake Form if contract is required.
4. Do not start vendor work without PO.

7) Implementation and change control

- This playbook is reviewed annually and after any material process or system change (ERP, CMS, procurement tooling). Suggested changes should be submitted using the Finance Policy Change Request form.
- Major process changes require Finance, Legal, Procurement, and Security approval and a 30-day transition window to allow stakeholder training.

Appendix A — Common scenarios and examples

Example 1: Dedicated capacity contract with annual prepayment
- Contract value: $600,000 for a 12-month committed capacity term, invoiced annually in advance -> On receipt of cash, book $600,000 to deferred revenue and recognize $50,000 monthly over 12 months.

Example 2: Monthly metered API customer with usage discounts
- Contract: standard MSA + monthly usage; invoice generated monthly in arrears. If a customer has a committed minimum plus overage, split fixed minimum to be recognized ratably and overage recognized as consumed.

Contact and support

- For process questions, contact Finance Operations: finance-ops@redwood-inference.com
- For contract routing and legal questions: legal-contracts@redwood-inference.com
- Procurement help: procurement@redwood-inference.com
